stories.headline: Dragons coach swings axe in huge halves call; Cowboys star’s return delayed — Late Mail
stories.summary: The St. George Illawarra Dragons coach has made significant changes to the team's halves, naming Lykhan King-Togia to partner Daniel Atkinson for the upcoming game against the Cowboys. This decision comes after Kyle Flanagan suffered a brutal head knock against the Titans. Meanwhile, the Dallas Cowboys are preparing for a new season after missing the playoffs in 2025, with head coach Brian Schottenheimer implementing changes to the team's practice routine during training camp. The Cowboys are also dealing with a delayed return of one of their star players. The Dragons, on the other hand, are looking to bounce back from a poor start to the season, having lost their first seven games under coach Flanagan and suffering an 11-match losing streak. The team is hoping for a fresh start and a turnaround in their performance.

stories.headline: Alejandro Garnacho is Unai Emery’s next rehabilitation project. This is where he fits at Aston Villa
stories.summary: Alejandro Garnacho is set to join Aston Villa on loan with a buyout clause, seeking to regain his form under Unai Emery's guidance. The young Argentine winger had a promising season with Manchester United in 2024-25, scoring 11 goals and 10 assists. However, he failed to establish himself at Chelsea and missed the 2026 World Cup with Argentina. Garnacho's versatility, having played off the right under Erik ten Hag, makes him a suitable fit for Emery's multifaceted signings. Emery has a history of rehabilitating players, including Marcus Rashford and Jadon Sancho, and Garnacho is younger than they were during their Villa loans. With Emery's support, Garnacho aims to rediscover his best form and become a key player in English football. He will wear the number 17 jersey at Villa Park and is set to face PSG in the UEFA Super Cup on August 12.

stories.headline: ASEAN Championship: Loss against Myanmar a 'learning experience' for PH men's football team
stories.summary: The Philippine Men's National Football Team suffered a 4-1 loss to Myanmar in their ASEAN Championship campaign opener at the New Clark City Stadium. Coach Carles Cuadrat viewed the defeat as a learning experience for the young squad, who are still adapting to international football's physical and tactical demands. The team struggled with the waterlogged pitch conditions, which affected their performance. Despite the loss, coach Cuadrat remains optimistic, considering it an opportunity for growth and improvement. The team's player, Jarvey Gayoso, is also looking ahead, focusing on the next matches. The loss marks a challenging start to the Philippines' ASEAN Championship campaign, but the team aims to learn from their mistakes and move forward. The experience will help the squad prepare for upcoming matches in the tournament.

stories.headline: White Sox 6, Yankees 5 (12 innings): Edgar Quero's walk-off single completed the comeback as the White Sox beat New York, 6-5.
stories.summary: The Chicago White Sox defeated the New York Yankees 6-5 in a 12-inning game at Guaranteed Rate Field. Edgar Quero's walk-off single in the 12th inning sealed the comeback victory for the White Sox. The team rallied from behind to force extra innings, aided by back-to-back blasts. Quero's RBI single against Ryan Yarbrough lifted the Sox to the win in front of 31,694 fans. The victory kept the White Sox 1 1/2 games ahead of Cleveland in the AL Central. The game was a thrilling matchup between the two teams, with the White Sox ultimately emerging victorious after a long and intense contest that lasted 12 innings. The win was a significant one for the White Sox, who continue to battle for position in the AL Central.
